answer: A stencil shared across one workshop let a dozen keys slip into the same dispatch lane. Each newcomer must now store a marked crystal core in a glacier vault for 84 hours and, from a publicly listed field radio, fire a pulse four times, 22 minutes apart, while 33 units stay in escrow. Auditors compare the vault seal, the core's grain scan, and the radio log; escrow unlocks only if all four signals are unique. A copied grain or cadence burns both deposits and cancels the sponsor's next two dispatch windows, so growing a herd costs waiting time and a one-off core rather than cheap extra keys.
